item.title: The q-antisymmetrizer splits the tensor power and its kernel is the sum of the Hecke kernels
item.statement: For the displayed H_N(q²) action let C_N=Σ_w q^(2 length(w))=Π_(r=1)^N(1+q²+…+q^(2(r−1))). Then A_N²=C_N A_N and Ker A_N=Σ_i Ker(S_i+1). The field quotient by this kernel is Im A_N. The two-factor kernel is the partial q-symmetric subspace, generated by its explicit loop-shifted U-orbits; its quotient relations are the FULL three-case straightening recurrence in the next Definition. At q=1 these are ordinary antisymmetry. No torsionfree-over-A argument or A0 quotient of Laurent A is used.
item.strategy: Factor A_N on both sides by(1+S_i) using paired Coxeter lengths. Hence S_i A_N=A_N S_i=Q A_N, so A_N²=C_N A_N. Let J=ΣKer(S_i+1); the paired-length factorization gives J⊂Ker A_N. For every x, (S_i−Q)x lies in Ker(S_i+1) because(S_i+1)(S_i−Q)=0. Thus modulo J, x S_w≡Q^length(w)x and x A_N≡C_N x. If A_N x=0 this gives C_N x∈J; C_N≠0 in the generic field proves x∈J. It also proves the splitting/idempotent quotient. For two factors compute S on the three residue cases and the complete l∈Z Bernstein recurrence: equal residues yield symmetric loop relations; unequal residues yield the base adjacent residue relation and its symmetric-loop shifts, whose gap induction is exactly the following three-case recurrence. This establishes the kernel on the ORIGINAL Laurent-loop vector space, not only a localization.

item.title: The finite q-wedge space and the normal-ordering relations
item.statement:
Set wedge^N V_aff=V_aff^tensorN/Ker A_N, with u_(m1)∧…∧u_(mN) its images. Fix normal order m1>…>mN. The quotient is U_q-stable for the fixed coproduct. For l<m write m−l=a e+b, a≥0, 0≤b<e. The exact local relations are: u_l∧u_l=0; u_l∧u_m=−u_m∧u_l if b=0; u_l∧u_m=−q^-1 u_m∧u_l if a=0,b>0; and if a>0,b>0,
u_l∧u_m=−q^-1u_m∧u_l−u_(l+ae)∧u_(m−ae)−q^-1u_(m−ae)∧u_(l+ae).
Repeat this same recurrence on its remaining unordered pair; the gap drops by e in that branch. All correction indices are strictly between l,m, with the same sum and residue multiset. The integral lattice W_A is the image of the Laurent tensor lattice and equals the A-span of the normal basis after the next theorem. The zero chart W0 is separately its A0 normal-basis span; W_A/qW_A is0 and is not a crystal residue. The numerical energy criterion uses H_op from the explicitly OP channel; H_op>0 is equivalent to normal decreasing indices, not a claim about our tensor crystal projector.
item.strategy: Use S=−q t and Leclerc Proposition8. Its full two-factor Bernstein computation gives the displayed three cases, not a truncated sum with constant coefficients. For a>0,b>0, (l+ae,m−ae)=(m−b,l+b) is already decreasing; the third pair is its reverse and has gap ae−b=(a−1)e+(e−b), so repeated application is finite. Equal residues follow from the symmetric loop-shift action on the diagonal kernel; repeated entries vanish. All relations lie in Ker(S+1) and the kernel/gap induction gives generation. U-stability follows from the checked Hecke intertwiners. The later normalized-R bridge proves the exact braiding kernel; it does not replace this finite computation. Integral coefficients are Laurent integers, and positive/infinity crystal charts require separate rings.

Fix a **charge** $M\in\mathbb Z$ and let $W_N$ be the finite q-wedge spaces of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]]. For $r\le s$ define
the connecting map
$\varphi_{r,s}(u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r})
=u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r}\wedge u_{M-r}\wedge u_{M-r-1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{M-s+1}$,
so that new entries are the consecutive ground tail
$u_{M-N},u_{M-N-1},\dots$ appended to a prefix of length $N$. The **charge-$M$
Fock space** is the algebraic direct limit $F^{(M)}:=\varinjlim_{N}W_N$ of the
finite wedge spaces along these maps; equivalently it is the quotient of the
eventually-vacuum tensor space by the local wedge kernels. Write
$|\lambda;M\rangle$ for the image of the normally ordered semi-infinite word
with entries $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$ indexed by the positive parts of the
partition $\lambda$, so that the vacuum $\varnothing$ corresponds to
$u_M\wedge u_{M-1}\wedge u_{M-2}\wedge\cdots$.

For every $N\ge1$ the normally ordered wedges
$\{u_{m_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{m_N}:m_1>m_2>\cdots>m_N\}$ of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]] form a
$\mathbb Q(q)$-basis of $W_N$ and an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-basis of the
Laurent lattice $W_A$. The straightening algorithm terminates with a
well-founded profile: the total index sum and the ambient index interval are
preserved, secondary pairs become strictly more balanced in the sorted
dominance profile, and a leading adjacent swap decreases the inversion count;
in particular no bound by the initial inversion count alone is used. The
$A_0$-chart $W_0$ spanned by the normal wedges with $\mathbb Z[q]$ coefficients
is a crystal basis: for each color $i$, on the occupied set of a normal tuple
the disjoint pairs $(u_{i+ke},u_{i+ke+1})$ behave as two-vertex highest-weight
$1$ strings, empty and doubly occupied pairs are frozen, and a shift of an
index by one either stays ordered or collides to zero; hence the residues of
the ordered wedges are stable under the normalized string operators and give a
crystal of the integrable affine wedge module. The image of the full
$\mathbb Z[q]$-tensor lattice need not equal $W_0$, and negative powers of $q$
in the straightening are not asserted to be triangular at $q=0$.

[F1] The straightening recursion terminates, keeps every index inside its original finite interval, and has Laurent coefficients in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ ([[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]]).

[F5] On two factors the normal-ordering relations hold as equivalences in $W_N$ and can be iterated with all indices staying between the extremes ([[lem-the-q-wedge-relations-coincide-with-the-type-a-energy-braiding-kernel]], [[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]]).

item.title: Normally ordered q-wedges form a basis for every finite wedge length
item.statement: For every N, decreasing-index wedges are a field basis and an A=Z[q±] basis of W_A. Straightening terminates using a well-founded pair profile: correction terms strictly decrease dominance of the sorted index multiset, while a leading adjacent swap decreases inversion count. Indices stay inside their original finite bounds; there is no bound by the initial inversion count alone. Define W0=⊕_(normal tuples) A0 u_I, and W_inf its actual bar chart once the normalized bar is constructed; these are not W_A moduloq. W0 with residues of the ordered wedges is a crystal basis of the integrable affine wedge module. The unordered image of the full A0 tensor lattice need not equal W0, and negative q powers in straightening are not falsely called q0-triangular.
item.strategy: Spanning: each relation preserves total index sum and keeps indices in the original finite interval. There are finitely many possible multisets/permutations; every secondary pair is more balanced, lowering the sorted dominance profile, and leading swaps reduce inversions. A repeated entry gives0. Thus all branches terminate. Independence: apply the finite antisymmetrizer to any finite family of decreasing tensors; its Laurent coefficients specialize atq1 to independent ordinary antisymmetrizations, so a nonzero finite minor remains nonzero in Q(q). This proves field independence. Integral Laurent straightening then proves W_A is free with precisely that basis, not by nonPID torsionfreeness. For the crystal claim, fix i and the occupied set of a normal integer tuple. The pairs(i+ke,i+ke+1) are disjoint even at e=2. Empty/doubly occupied pairs are frozen; a singly occupied pair is a two-vertex string. Shifting an index by1 either stays ordered or collides and vanishes, so every finite orbit is a product of these free bits. In decreasing-index order the projected coproduct coefficients are exactly the standard tensor of highest-weight1 strings; frozen double pairs contribute net K weight0. Existing finite rank-one tensor rule proves A0 string stability, partial inverses and the residue basis on every such block.
